parts.title: Orientation
parts.summary: What Swahili is and which Swahili this guide teaches, the idea that runs through its grammar (noun classes and agreement, and the verb as a template of slots), and how to read the guide.

parts.title: Sounds and spelling
parts.summary: Five vowels and open syllables, the consonants and digraphs, prenasalised consonants and ng', the Arabic-derived sounds, penultimate stress, and what happens when a prefix meets a vowel.

parts.title: The simplest sentences
parts.summary: People nouns and the copula ni, the first verb (subject prefix, -na-, root, final vowel), the negative present, yes-no questions, being somewhere, having and 'there is', commands and greetings.

parts.title: Noun classes and agreement
parts.summary: The class system pair by pair, each with its agreement on verbs and adjectives; animate agreement; possessives; the -a of association; demonstratives; locative classes; pronouns and word order; the full agreement map.

parts.title: The verb template
parts.summary: The slots of the verb, the tenses (-li-, -ta-, -me-, -ja-), short verbs, object prefixes and the reflexive, the subjunctive and its uses, the infinitive, the habitual hu-, -ki-, narrative -ka-, compound tenses, 'already' and 'still', and choosing a tense.

parts.title: Modifying and linking
parts.summary: Adjective types, -enye and -a phrases, numbers, time and dates, -ote and its relatives, comparison, adverbs, prepositions, conjunctions, question words, and building words by class prefix and derivation.

parts.title: Complex sentences
parts.summary: Relative clauses in all their forms (amba-, the relative infix, object, general and negative relatives, relatives of 'be' and 'have', when/where/how), focus with ndi-, that-clauses and reported speech, purpose, time, conditions, concession and negative polarity.

parts.title: Verb extensions and special topics
parts.summary: The extensions slot: applicative, passive, causative, stative, reciprocal, reversive and stacking; the -a- tense and spoken shortcuts; respect and register; varieties, old texts and the standard; loanwords.

parts.title: Reading real texts
parts.summary: Six graded passages: proverbs, a Zanzibar folktale recorded in 1870 (two lessons), the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (Articles 1 and 3 to 5), Swahili Wikipedia on Kiswahili, and a capstone reading of the Tanzanian national anthem, Mungu ibariki Afrika.

parts.title: Reference
parts.summary: Agreement tables, the verb template chart and verb tables, core vocabulary, glossary of terms and abbreviations, annotated bibliography.

lessons.title: What Swahili is
lessons.point: Place Swahili in space, history and family, and know which Swahili this guide teaches

lessons.title: The organising idea: noun classes, agreement and the verb template
lessons.point: See how one noun's class prefix echoes through a whole sentence, and how every verb is built from slots in a fixed order

lessons.title: How to use this guide
lessons.point: Read the glosses (class numbers, SM and OM, tense markers), the slot notation and the confidence dots, and know where the facts come from

lessons.title: Five vowels and open syllables
lessons.point: Pronounce the five vowels and split any word into syllables, including syllabic m and n

lessons.title: Consonants and the digraphs ch, sh, ny, ng'
lessons.point: Pronounce the consonants and read the digraphs, knowing which letters Swahili does not use

lessons.title: mb, nd, nj, ng: nasal before consonant
lessons.point: Say nasal-plus-consonant clusters correctly, know when the nasal is a syllable of its own, and tell ng from ng'

lessons.title: Sounds from Arabic: dh, th, gh, kh
lessons.point: Pronounce the Arabic-derived consonants and recognise the common substitutions you will hear

lessons.title: Stress on the second-to-last syllable
lessons.point: Place the stress in any word, see it move as prefixes and suffixes are added, and spot the few exceptions

lessons.title: When a prefix meets a vowel
lessons.point: Predict mw-, w-, y-, ch-, vy- and merged vowels where a prefix meets a vowel-initial stem, the key to reading agreement prefixes

lessons.title: People: m- and wa-, and saying who someone is with ni
lessons.point: Say who or what someone is with ni and si, using the personal pronouns and the singular and plural of people nouns

lessons.title: The first verb: subject prefix, -na- and the root
lessons.point: Build present-tense verbs like ninasoma 'I am reading' for every person, and cite verbs by their ku- form

lessons.title: Saying 'not': the negative present
lessons.point: Negate present verbs with the negative subject prefixes and the final -i

lessons.title: Yes-no questions and answers
lessons.point: Ask yes-no questions with intonation and je, and answer with ndiyo, hapana and la

lessons.title: Being somewhere: -po, -ko, -mo
lessons.point: Say where someone is with nipo, yuko, wamo and their negatives

lessons.title: Having and 'there is': nina, kuna, hakuna
lessons.point: Say what someone has and what there is or is not, with a subject prefix plus na

lessons.title: Commands: soma! someni!
lessons.point: Give commands to one person or several, including the irregular njoo, nenda and lete

lessons.title: Greetings: hujambo, habari, shikamoo
lessons.point: Greet and answer correctly, and see why hujambo is built like a negative verb

lessons.title: What a noun class is
lessons.point: Understand classes as prefix pairs with their own agreement, and know both the numbers and the school names (ki-vi, m-mi)

lessons.title: Classes 7 and 8: ki- and vi-
lessons.point: Use ki-/vi- nouns with matching subject prefixes on the verb, including ch- and vy- before vowels

lessons.title: Adjectives agree: the adjective prefix
lessons.point: Put an adjective after its noun with the right prefix, and use adjectives as predicates with ni

lessons.title: Classes 3 and 4: m- and mi-
lessons.point: Use trees, body parts and natural forces with u- and i- agreement on verbs and m-/mi- on adjectives

lessons.title: Classes 5 and 6: ji-, zero and ma-
lessons.point: Handle class 5 nouns with no visible prefix, ma- plurals and mass nouns, and li-/ya- agreement

lessons.title: Classes 9 and 10: the nasal class
lessons.point: Predict the nasal prefix on nouns and adjectives, and agree with i- and zi- when the noun itself does not change

lessons.title: Classes 11 and 14: u- nouns, their plurals and abstracts
lessons.point: Form plurals of u- nouns in class 10, and use class 14 abstracts like uhuru and utoto

lessons.title: People and animals in any class: animate agreement
lessons.point: Use class 1 and 2 agreement for every noun that names a person or animal, whatever its own prefix

lessons.title: Possessives: -angu, -ako, -ake
lessons.point: Say my, your, his, our and their with the possessive stem and the right class prefix, including the kin-term pattern

lessons.title: 'Of': the -a of association
lessons.point: Link two nouns with cha, la, ya, za, wa, kwa, and build compound nouns

lessons.title: This, that and that one: demonstratives
lessons.point: Form and choose the three demonstratives (huyu, yule, huyo) for every class

lessons.title: Places: -ni and classes 16, 17 and 18
lessons.point: Make locative nouns with -ni and agree with them through pa-, ku- and mu-

lessons.title: Pronouns, word order and the short forms with na
lessons.point: Drop pronouns the verb already shows, use them for emphasis, keep neutral SVO order, and say 'with me', 'and it' with nami, naye, nacho

lessons.title: The agreement map: all concords in one table
lessons.point: Look up the noun, adjective, subject, possessive, -a and demonstrative forms of every class, and see what predicts them

lessons.title: The verb template: slots in a fixed order
lessons.point: Name the slots (subject, tense, relative, object, root, extension, final vowel) and place every marker you know in them

lessons.title: The past: -li- and negative -ku-
lessons.point: Say what happened and what did not happen

lessons.title: The future: -ta-
lessons.point: Say what will and will not happen, and recognise the spoken negative -to-

lessons.title: Short verbs and the stress-carrying ku: kula, kunywa, kuja
lessons.point: Conjugate two-syllable verbs and kwenda, keeping ku- exactly where the stress needs it

lessons.title: The perfect -me- and 'not yet' -ja-
lessons.point: Say what has happened and still matters, and what has not happened yet

lessons.title: States through the perfect: nimechoka, amelala
lessons.point: Express being tired, asleep, full, dressed or seated, which Swahili says with change-of-state verbs in -me-

lessons.title: Object prefixes I: me, you, him, us, them
lessons.point: Put -ni-, -ku-, -m(w)-, -tu-, -wa- in the object slot and mark 'you all' with -eni

lessons.title: Object prefixes II: things, definiteness and -ji- 'self'
lessons.point: Use class object prefixes, know when an object prefix is needed or adds definiteness, and make reflexives with -ji-

lessons.title: The subjunctive: -e for wishes, requests and 'let's'
lessons.point: Form the subjunctive and use it for polite requests, suggestions, commands with objects, and 'let's'

lessons.title: Using the subjunctive: wanting, needing, telling and 'don't'
lessons.point: Use the subjunctive after -taka, lazima and -ambia, and make prohibitions with -si-

lessons.title: The infinitive: kusoma as verb and noun (class 15)
lessons.point: Use ku- forms after verbs like -penda and -weza, negate them with kuto-, and treat them as class 15 nouns

lessons.title: The habitual hu-: what usually happens
lessons.point: Say what regularly or generally happens with hu-, and know why it is common in proverbs and rare in conversation

lessons.title: -ki-: while, if, when
lessons.point: Use -ki- for background actions, conditions and participle-like 'doing' forms

lessons.title: -ka-: telling a story, 'and then'
lessons.point: Chain past events with -ka- after an opening -li-, and use -ka- with the subjunctive for 'go and do'

lessons.title: Compound tenses with kuwa: was doing, had done, will have done
lessons.point: Shift the present, perfect and -ki- forms into past and future with an inflected kuwa

lessons.title: Already and still: -sha-, -ngali, bado
lessons.point: Say 'already' with -mesha- and -sha-, 'still' with -ngali and bado, and combine them with the tenses

lessons.title: Choosing a tense
lessons.point: Decide between -na-, hu-, -me-, -li-, -ka-, -ki- and -ta- for a given meaning, and build any verb slot by slot

lessons.title: Adjectives with vowel stems, irregular and invariable adjectives
lessons.point: Inflect -ema, -ingi, -ekundu, -pya and the other awkward adjectives, and use invariable ones like safi and ghali

lessons.title: Describing without adjectives: -enye and -a phrases
lessons.point: Say 'having', 'strong', 'modern' with -enye + noun and -a + noun, the commonest ways to describe

lessons.title: Numbers 1 to 10 and agreement
lessons.point: Count and quantify with the agreeing numbers (-moja, -wili, -tatu, -nne, -tano, -nane) and the invariable ones (sita, saba, tisa, kumi)

lessons.title: Bigger numbers, Swahili time, days and dates
lessons.point: Count past ten, tell the time in Swahili hours (saa mbili is 8 o'clock), and name days, months and years

lessons.title: All, any, self, other, which: -ote, -o-ote, -enyewe, -ingine, -pi
lessons.point: Use the words that take subject-type prefixes, and tell 'all of us' (sote) from 'both of us' (sisi wote)

lessons.title: Comparison: kuliko, zaidi, kushinda
lessons.point: Say bigger than, the biggest, as big as, with kuliko, zaidi ya, -shinda and -pita

lessons.title: Adverbs: vizuri, kwa haraka, polepole
lessons.point: Make adverbs with vi- and kwa, use the common place and time adverbs, and reduplicate for manner

lessons.title: Prepositions: na, kwa, katika, kwenye and the -a compounds
lessons.point: Express place, means and company with na, kwa, katika, kwenye and juu ya, chini ya, ndani ya, karibu na

lessons.title: Joining words: na, au, lakini, kisha, kwa sababu
lessons.point: Join words and clauses, and see why na joins nouns but not clauses in careful style

lessons.title: Question words: nani, nini, wapi, lini, -pi, -ngapi, gani
lessons.point: Ask content questions with the question word in place, and use the verb endings -je and -ni

lessons.title: Building words: derived nouns and class shift
lessons.point: Derive nouns from verbs (mwandishi, mchezo, uandishi), and move nouns between classes to make them small, big, abstract or a language name

lessons.title: Relative clauses I: amba- and the o of reference
lessons.point: Make 'who, which, that' clauses with ambaye, ambacho and the rest for every class

lessons.title: Relative clauses II: the relative inside the verb
lessons.point: Build aliyekuja, kinachofuata, nitakachosoma with -li-, -na- and -taka- plus the relative marker

lessons.title: Relative clauses III: object relatives
lessons.point: Relativise objects (kitabu nilichokisoma), know when the object prefix appears, and keep track of two classes in one verb

lessons.title: Relative clauses IV: the general relative and the negative relative
lessons.point: Read timeless relatives like asemaye and wakaao, and make negative relatives with -si- (asiyejua)

lessons.title: Who is, which has: relatives of 'be' and 'have'
lessons.point: Use aliye, kilicho, walio na and nilicho nacho for 'who is' and 'which I have'

lessons.title: When, where, how: -po-, -ko-, -mo-, -vyo- relatives
lessons.point: Make time, place and manner clauses (alipofika 'when he arrived', anavyosema 'as he says')

lessons.title: It is he who: ndiye, ndicho and siye
lessons.point: Focus a person or thing with ndi- plus the reference form, and deny it with si-

lessons.title: That-clauses and reported speech: kwamba, kuwa, kama
lessons.point: Report statements, yes-no questions (kama 'whether') and commands, and shift persons in reported speech

lessons.title: Purpose: ili, the subjunctive and kwa ajili ya
lessons.point: Say 'in order to' and 'so that' with ili and the subjunctive, the infinitive and kwa ajili ya

lessons.title: Time clauses: before, after, until, since, while
lessons.point: Join events in time with -po-, baada ya, kabla ya, mpaka, tangu and -ki-

lessons.title: Real conditions: -ki-, -sipo-, kama, ikiwa
lessons.point: Say 'if' and 'unless' for open conditions with -ki-, -sipo- and the if-words

lessons.title: Hypothetical conditions: -nge- and -ngali-
lessons.point: Say 'would' and 'would have' with -nge-, -ngali- and the negatives -singe-, -singali-

lessons.title: Because, although, even if
lessons.point: Give reasons and concessions with kwa sababu, kwa kuwa, ingawa, ijapokuwa, hata kama

lessons.title: Ever, never, neither nor: -wahi, kamwe, wala
lessons.point: Say 'have you ever', 'never' and 'neither... nor', and handle negation across clauses

lessons.title: Verb extensions: one root, many verbs
lessons.point: See how suffixes between root and final vowel change who does what to whom, and predict the i/e harmony they follow

lessons.title: The applicative I: doing for, to and at
lessons.point: Add -i-/-e- (-li-/-le-) to bring a beneficiary, goal or place into the verb (nunulia, andikia)

lessons.title: The applicative II: reason, instrument, direction and two objects
lessons.point: Use applicatives for 'why', 'with what', 'towards' and with two objects, and read lexicalised applicatives

lessons.title: The passive: -w- and -liw-, -lew-
lessons.point: Form passives for every verb shape and add the agent with na

lessons.title: Passives of applicatives and of 'give': nilipewa, aliandikiwa
lessons.point: Make the beneficiary the subject (I was given, he was written to), and handle the short-verb passives (-liwa, -pewa, -nywewa)

lessons.title: The causative I: -ish-, -esh- and -iz-, -ez-
lessons.point: Make someone do something or make something happen (somesha 'teach', chelewesha 'delay')

lessons.title: The causative II: sound-change causatives and verbs from adjectives and nouns
lessons.point: Recognise -sha from -ka and -za from vowel stems (amsha, jaza), and derive verbs like safisha and fupisha

lessons.title: The stative: -ik-, -ek- 'get broken', 'be doable'
lessons.point: Use the stative for changes with no agent and for possibility (vunjika, eleweka, -lika 'be edible'), and contrast it with the passive

lessons.title: The reciprocal -an-: each other
lessons.point: Say 'each other' and 'with each other', with plural subjects or a na-phrase

lessons.title: Reversives, frozen extensions and stacking
lessons.point: Recognise reversive -u-/-o- (fungua), static -am- and reduplicated verbs, and read stacked extensions in the right order

lessons.title: The -a- tense and spoken shortcuts: nasoma, twaenda, -ga
lessons.point: Read the gnomic -a- tense and its contracted prefixes, the dropped ni- of speech, and the colloquial habitual -ga

lessons.title: Respect, politeness and register
lessons.point: Address elders and strangers correctly (shikamoo, mzee, bwana, bibi), soften requests, and recognise the formal written style

lessons.title: Varieties, old texts and the standard
lessons.point: Know what the standard is based on and how it was fixed, recognise Kenyan, coastal, Congo and Sheng forms, and know how Ajami script and utenzi verse work

lessons.title: Loanwords: how Arabic, English and other words fit the classes
lessons.point: See how loans are given classes and verb shapes (kitabu/vitabu, mwalimu/walimu, -fikiri), and recognise the Arabic and English layers

lessons.title: Reading 1: proverbs (methali)
lessons.point: Read eight proverbs, each a full sentence in the copula, the habitual, the imperative, -enye or -sipo-

lessons.title: Reading 2: the monkey and the shark (Zanzibar, 1870), part 1
lessons.point: Read the opening of a tale recorded by Steere in Zanzibar: dialogue, -ka- narrative and nineteenth-century spellings

lessons.title: Reading 3: the washerman's donkey (Zanzibar, 1870), part 2
lessons.point: Read the tale within the tale to its end, following the subjects through long -ka- chains

lessons.title: Reading 4: the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, Articles 1 and 3 to 5
lessons.point: Read formal written Swahili: perfects and passives, kila, and negative subjunctives of prohibition (asifanywe, asiteswe)

lessons.title: Reading 5: Swahili Wikipedia on Kiswahili
lessons.point: Read modern expository prose with relatives, the habitual, -ki- and passives

lessons.title: Reading 6 (capstone): Mungu ibariki Afrika, the Tanzanian national anthem
lessons.point: Read the whole anthem line by line: imperatives with object prefixes on a loan verb, possessives, demonstratives, the causative dumisha

lessons.title: Agreement tables
lessons.point: Look up every concord of every class: noun, adjective, subject, object, possessive, -a, demonstrative, relative, -ote, -enye

lessons.title: The verb template chart and verb tables
lessons.point: See every verb marker in its slot, with positive and negative forms of model verbs of each shape (soma, la, jibu)

lessons.title: Core vocabulary
lessons.point: Find every word taught in the guide with its class or verb shape and the lesson that introduces it

lessons.title: Glossary of terms and abbreviations
lessons.point: Look up every grammatical term and gloss abbreviation

lessons.title: Annotated bibliography
lessons.point: Know which grammars, dictionaries, courses and corpora to use next
